build_spec:
# Atlas Weekly Recap — Blueprint

## Overview

Cron-driven weekly recap. Every Sunday at the configured local time, reads the past week's archive (written by digest + capture), ranks items per bucket, runs a pattern-detection LLM pass, composes a Team_bot_a-style recap, and posts it to the configured Telegram group.

Depends on p-7b26ba5e for atlas_lib (archive read, composer, config, telegram_api). Also reads optout.json from p-df9d99a3 (if present) to suppress opted-out items.

## File layout

```
scripts/
  atlas_recap.py             ← main CLI: send | preview | status
  atlas-recap-cron.sh        ← cron trigger (rendered below)
recap/
  {YYYY-WW}.md               ← one file per ISO week (local audit)
/Library/LaunchDaemons/
  com.{bot_id}.atlas-weekly-recap.plist  ← weekly trigger (rendered below)
```

## Per-file specs

### scripts/atlas_recap.py
- **Purpose:** Main CLI. Subcommands: `send` (full pipeline), `preview` (skip Telegram post + recap log write), `status` (read latest recap file).
- **Inputs:** flags `--bot-id`, `--chat-id`, `--week ISO_YEAR-WNN` (default = previous 7 days), `--detail concise|standard|detailed`, `--max-items-per-bucket N`.
- **send pipeline:**
  1. Resolve target ISO week (from `--week` or default to previous 7 days ending now).
  2. Read archive entries in that range via `atlas_lib.archive.items_in_range(start, end, archive_dir)`.
  3. Filter out items whose URL is in `atlas/optout.json` (if present).
  4. If filtered set has < 3 items, emit `RECAP_EMPTY: <iso_week>` and exit 0.
  5. Rank within each bucket via composite score (source_weight × recency_decay × similar_domain_count); pick top N per bucket.
  6. Run pattern-detection LLM pass on top items (titles + buckets + sources, NO full bodies).
  7. Compose recap via `atlas_lib.composer.compose_recap(items, patterns, detail, week_start, week_end)`.
  8. Post via `atlas_lib.telegram_api.send_message`.
  9. Write `recap/{YYYY-WW}.md` with posted_at header + recap text + source archive IDs.
 10. Emit `RECAP_SENT: <iso_week> <total_items>`.
- **preview pipeline:** same up through compose; print to stdout; do NOT post or write recap file.
- **status:** read recap/ dir; print latest posted week + first line, or 'no recaps posted yet'.
- **First-run safety:** if archive_dir doesn't exist or has 0 items, emit RECAP_EMPTY.

### scripts/atlas-recap-cron.sh
Bash trigger invoked by LaunchDaemon. Rendered as a `## FILE:` block below.

## Composite ranking score

```python
score = source_weight(item.source) * recency_decay(item.age_days) * dup_signal(item.domain, all_items)

# Source weights (default):
source_weights = {
    'anthropic-blog': 1.0, 'openai-blog': 1.0, 'google-blog-ai': 1.0,
    'openclaw-blog': 1.2, 'hn-frontpage': 0.8,
    'r-LocalLLaMA': 0.7, 'telegram-member': 0.7,
}
# github-release:<repo> → 0.9 (prefix match)
# brave-search:<query> → 0.6 (prefix match)

# Recency: 1.0 today, decays 0.1 per day, floor 0.4 at day 7+
recency = max(0.4, 1.0 - 0.1 * age_days)

# Dup signal: items in same bucket from same domain boost each other (cross-source confirmation)
similar = count_items_in_bucket_with_same_domain(item, all_items)
dup_signal = 1.0 + 0.2 * (similar - 1)
```

This surfaces items multiple sources are talking about (cross-source confirmation), penalizes single-source noise, and gracefully handles old items still in the week.

## Pattern detection prompt

Given top 15-25 items (titles + buckets + sources only — no full bodies):

> You are looking at the past week of items archived by Atlas, an OpenClaw / AI-agent ecosystem digest bot. Identify 1-3 patterns visible ACROSS items — themes that connect multiple items, not commentary on any single one.
>
> Items this week (title, bucket, source):
> {items}
>
> Rules:
> - Patterns are OBSERVATIONS, not recommendations.
> - If you see fewer than 2 items supporting a pattern, don't list it.
> - If you genuinely see nothing emergent, return {{"patterns": [], "confidence": 0.0}}.
>
> Return JSON only: {"patterns": ["...", "..."], "confidence": 0.0-1.0}
> If confidence < 0.6, return patterns: [].

If the LLM returns patterns: [] (or fails), the recap header is 'Quiet week — nothing emergent surfaced. Highlights below.' rather than fabricated themes.

## Recap format (Team_bot_a-style)

```
📰 Atlas weekly recap — week of {start_date} to {end_date} ({YYYY-WW})
{total} item(s) archived this week.

🧭 Patterns this week
• {pattern 1}
• {pattern 2}
(or: 'Quiet week — nothing emergent surfaced.')

⚔️ Competitive landscape (top {n})
• {title} ({source}) — {short-url}
…

🛠 New tools (top {n})
…

🏆 Use cases (top {n})
…

📚 Case studies (top {n})
…

⚠️ Warnings (top {n})
…

— Full archive in @atlas's workspace; /ask for focused research; /optout <link> to remove an item.
```

Buckets with 0 items omitted entirely. Pattern section mandatory (either content or 'quiet week' note).

## Configuration file templates

## FILE: scripts/atlas-recap-cron.sh
```bash
#!/bin/bash
# atlas-recap-cron.sh — weekly-recap cron trigger. Installed by atlas-weekly-recap.
WORKSPACE="/Users/{bot_id}/.openclaw/workspace"
LOGFILE="/tmp/{bot_id}-atlas-recap.log"

python3 "$WORKSPACE/scripts/atlas_recap.py" send \
  --bot-id "{bot_id}" \
  --chat-id "{telegram_chat_id}" \
  --detail "{recap_detail}" \
  >> "$LOGFILE" 2>&1

exit 0
```

## FILE: /Library/LaunchDaemons/com.{bot_id}.atlas-weekly-recap.plist
```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!DOCTYPE plist PUBLIC "-//Apple//DTD PLIST 1.0//EN"
  "http://www.apple.com/DTDs/PropertyList-1.0.dtd">
<plist version="1.0">
<dict>
  <key>Label</key>
  <string>com.{bot_id}.atlas-weekly-recap</string>
  <key>UserName</key>
  <string>{bot_id}</string>
  <key>GroupName</key>
  <string>staff</string>
  <key>ProgramArguments</key>
  <array>
    <string>/bin/bash</string>
    <string>/Users/{bot_id}/.openclaw/workspace/scripts/atlas-recap-cron.sh</string>
  </array>
  <key>EnvironmentVariables</key>
  <dict>
    <key>TZ</key>
    <string>{briefing_tz_env}</string>
  </dict>
  <key>StartCalendarInterval</key>
  <dict>
    <key>Weekday</key>
    <integer>0</integer>
    <key>Hour</key>
    <integer>{briefing_hour}</integer>
    <key>Minute</key>
    <integer>{briefing_minute}</integer>
  </dict>
  <key>StandardOutPath</key>
  <string>/tmp/{bot_id}-atlas-recap-out.log</string>
  <key>StandardErrorPath</key>
  <string>/tmp/{bot_id}-atlas-recap-err.log</string>
  <key>RunAtLoad</key>
  <false/>
</dict>
</plist>
```

Note: Weekday=0 = Sunday in launchd. Hour/Minute are derived from a 'recap_time' template var by the provisioner the same way digest uses briefing_time. Until v7 introduces multi-cron-per-app, this app uses its own briefing_time slot.

## Integration with sibling apps

Reads from `archive/` (shared state owned by p-7b26ba5e, also written by p-df9d99a3). Read-only — recap never modifies the archive.

Reads `atlas/optout.json` if present (owned by p-df9d99a3). The check happens at compose time, not just at read time — so even if a member opts out mid-week, the recap won't include their items.

No write conflicts with siblings: recap only writes to its own `recap/` directory.

## Recursive LLM concerns

One LLM purpose (pattern detection). Per recursive_llm contract: exponential backoff max 3, on permanent failure fall back to 'quiet week' header and still ship the recap. The fallback is acceptable because the bucket sections are still useful without patterns.

## Test surface

Validate:
- `atlas_recap.py preview --week <some-week-with-items>` produces formatted recap with at least one bucket section.
- A week with < 3 archived items produces RECAP_EMPTY.
- Items in atlas/optout.json do not appear in the preview output.
- `atlas_recap.py status` against a workspace with no posted recaps yet returns 'no recaps posted yet' (no crash).
- Plist passes `plutil -lint` after rendering.

## What NOT to include

- No interactive surface — purely cron-driven.
- No re-classification — uses bucket from archive at capture time.
- No re-fetching of source articles.
- No multi-week aggregation in this app — one ISO week per run.
- No member-specific output — recap is the same for everyone in the group.
